bodyHtml:
NDT training in St. Louis: how it works for St. Louis employers and technicians

Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for St. Louis and the Metro East at Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory is taught live online and practical training runs onsite at your facility, on either side of the Mississippi, under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you under its written practice after training, documented experience, examinations and a vision test.

St. Louis is a two-state inspection market. On the Missouri side sit military aircraft production, automotive assembly, breweries, chemical and pharmaceutical plants and a large base of fabrication and machine shops. Across the river in Illinois, the Metro East adds a major refinery, steelmaking, chemical plants, rail yards and barge terminals. Between them runs the inland waterway system, with its barges, fleeting areas, terminals and bridges. For technicians, that variety means real choice. For employers, it means two different state regulatory regimes for radiography, different customer requirements, and inspection crews whose training has to satisfy them all.

Atlantis does not have a physical training centre in St. Louis, Clayton, Chesterfield, Belleville or anywhere else. Formal classroom training is taught live online by an instructor in real time; practical training and practical examinations are delivered onsite at the employer's own facility, using its equipment, reference standards and specimens. Under SNT-TC-1A, a training course does not certify anyone by itself. The employer certifies its own personnel against its written practice, using a Level III to administer examinations.

The St. Louis enquiries we see come from aerospace and defence suppliers formalising PT, MT and ET for prime contractors; fabrication and mechanical contractors needing Level II UT or RT for pressure and piping work; refinery and chemical-plant contractors preparing for turnarounds in the Metro East; barge, rail and heavy-equipment repair shops needing MT and UT; career changers from welding, machining and the military; and Level IIs preparing for the ASNT Level III examinations. The sections below are written to help each of them plan properly.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in St. Louis

All eight methods are available to St. Louis employers and technicians at Level I and II, with Level III examination preparation for experienced candidates. The third column shows typical uses in the St. Louis region, as planning context only.

MethodLevelsWhat St. Louis employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic testing (UT)I, II, III prepWeld examination in pressure and structural fabrication, refinery and chemical-plant thickness surveys, aerospace forgings and composites, rail axles and wheelsNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
Phased array UT (PAUT)II, III prepRefinery and chemical-plant weld and corrosion work, heavy fabrication and bridge-steel weldsConventional UT Level II recommended
Time-of-flight diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepFlaw sizing on thick vessel and heavy-structure welds during turnarounds and fabricationConventional UT Level II recommended
Radiographic testing (RT)I, II, III prepPipe and vessel welds for mechanical contractors and fabricators, castings, refinery pipingNone for Level I; radiation-safety certification is a separate regulatory requirement
Magnetic particle testing (MT)I, II, III prepFerrous aerospace and defence parts, barge and railcar structure, lifting gear, structural and bridge weldsNone for Level I
Liquid penetrant testing (PT)I, II, III prepAluminium and titanium aerospace parts, stainless piping in breweries, pharma and chemical plantsNone for Level I
Visual testing (VT)I, II, III prepWeld and structural inspection across fabrication, construction, barge and plant workNone for Level I
Eddy current testing (ET)I, II, III prepAircraft fastener holes and surface cracks, conductivity checks, heat-exchanger tubing in refineries and chemical plantsNone for Level I; PT or MT background helps

Choosing a first method in St. Louis. For someone targeting the aerospace and defence supply chain around Lambert airport and in St. Charles County, PT and MT are typical entry methods, with ET and UT the methods that lead to more specialised roles. For someone targeting fabrication, mechanical contracting or the Metro East refinery and chemical plants, VT and MT are the usual first steps and UT the method that opens up Level II weld and thickness work. RT remains in demand among piping and pressure-vessel contractors, but comes with separate radiation-safety requirements. PAUT and TOFD make sense after conventional UT Level II, especially for technicians who want turnaround work.

Each Atlantis method course covers principles and physics, equipment and materials, calibration and reference standards, technique selection, detecting and evaluating indications, applying acceptance criteria, and reporting. Level II extends to setting up techniques from written procedures, evaluating independently and guiding Level I personnel. See NDT training for the full course list and ASNT Level III training for the Level III route.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in St. Louis, step by step

These are the standard SNT-TC-1A steps. Your employer's written practice sets the details and may require more than the recommended minimums. The recommended classroom and experience hours by method and level are in our training requirements matrix.

  1. Confirm your governing written practice. A defence supplier in Hazelwood, a mechanical contractor in Fenton and a refinery contractor in Wood River may all be SNT-TC-1A employers with very different documents and customer overlays.
  2. Complete formal classroom training. Take the method course for your target level and keep the course outline, hours, dates and instructor details.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Work under certified supervision and record dates, techniques, items examined and hours, signed off as you go.
  4. General examination. A written test on method principles under the authority of a Level III.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on your employer's equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination. A hands-on test on real specimens covering set-up, calibration, detection, evaluation and reporting.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast differentiation, with near vision re-checked at least annually.
  8. Employer certification. Written certification by the employer for the method and level, valid with that employer.
  9. Maintain and recertify. Keep vision current, maintain continuity, and recertify at the written practice interval. A new employer certifies you under its own written practice and may credit documented prior training and experience.

See our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide for more on each step and on what auditors expect.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for St. Louis crews

Live online theory. Classroom content is taught in real time, with questions, worked examples and assessments. Crews spread between St. Charles, south county and the Illinois side can attend without crossing the river at rush hour, and sessions can be arranged in blocks that suit shift patterns. See the online NDT training page.

Onsite practical at your facility. Practical training and examinations are run at the employer's site, in Missouri or Illinois, using your equipment and representative specimens: aerospace detail parts for a supplier, pipe and plate welds for a contractor, barge or railcar weldments for a repair yard.

Scheduling around St. Louis workloads. Refinery and chemical-plant turnarounds in the Metro East pull large numbers of inspection technicians in concentrated periods; power-plant outages at regional coal, gas and nuclear stations do the same. Aerospace suppliers work to production rates, and river work is seasonal, with high and low water affecting barge and terminal maintenance. The best plan is to complete live-online theory in quieter weeks and schedule onsite practicals so technicians are certified ahead of the next turnaround or outage. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day, and multi-site employers can use our corporate NDT training programmes. Ask about onsite training for your St. Louis crew.

Where NDT technicians work in St. Louis

Aerospace and defence. Boeing's St. Louis operations produce the F-15EX, the T-7A trainer and the MQ-25, with the F/A-18 and munitions lines in the region, and a large new facility for next-generation combat aircraft has been built in north St. Louis County. Around them is a supply chain of machine shops, finishers, fabricators and composite shops. Aerospace and defence customers usually impose their own process specifications, and many require NAS 410 or EN 4179 qualification and Nadcap-accredited processes. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A-based and does not provide NAS 410 certification, so defence suppliers should use our method training and Level III support as part of their own qualification scheme and confirm what their prime requires.

Refining, chemicals and steel in the Metro East. The Wood River refinery complex at Roxana, chemical plants along the Illinois riverfront, steelmaking in Granite City and pipeline and fuel terminals around Hartford and East St. Louis generate heavy demand for UT thickness and weld examination, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT and ET of exchanger tubing. Process piping typically follows ASME B31.3, vessels ASME Section VIII and storage tanks API 650, with in-service inspection to API codes. Owner-side API 510, 570 or 653 inspectors are a separate certification that Atlantis does not offer.

Power generation. Ameren Missouri's Callaway Energy Center near Fulton is Missouri's nuclear plant, and coal and gas stations such as Labadie serve the region. Boiler and piping work follows ASME Section I and B31.1, and nuclear work adds its own quality-assurance and qualification rules. Outage seasons draw inspectors from the whole St. Louis labour pool.

River, barge and rail. The Port of St. Louis and the barge-building, fleeting and repair operations on the Mississippi and Illinois rivers use VT, MT and UT on hull structure, deck fittings and cargo systems. Railcar manufacturing and repair in the region, and major rail yards, use MT and UT on wheels, axles, couplers and car structure, often under Association of American Railroads requirements.

Manufacturing, breweries and pharma. Automotive assembly in Wentzville and its suppliers, one of the country's best-known breweries, and chemical and life-sciences plants use stainless process piping, pressure vessels and tanks, calling for PT, VT and UT. Structural fabricators weld to AWS D1.1, and Mississippi River bridges on the MoDOT and IDOT systems follow AWS D1.5 for bridge steel.

Radiography licensing: Missouri versus Illinois. This matters for St. Louis crews. Missouri is not an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography with radioactive sources in Missouri is licensed directly by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission under 10 CFR Part 34. Illinois is an Agreement State, and radioactive-material licensing there is handled by the Illinois Emergency Management Agency. A radiography company working on both sides of the river needs authorisation from both regulators, which usually means a primary licence from one and reciprocity with the other. Radiographers must hold radiation-safety certification, commonly ASNT IRRSP or an equivalent recognised programme. Electronic X-ray equipment is regulated at state level rather than by the NRC. Our RT course teaches the NDT method and interpretation; it does not replace radiation-safety training or certification.

St. Louis employers typically look for Level II in the relevant method, verifiable experience logs, a current vision record and, for aerospace, defence and nuclear work, the ability to work to a customer specification. For pay, see the NDT salary guide rather than local figures we cannot verify.

Level III services and written practices for St. Louis NDT companies

St. Louis has a deep base of mid-sized manufacturers and contractors whose inspection functions have grown over decades. Many operate with an older written practice that has not kept pace with the current edition of SNT-TC-1A, with a Level III who has retired, or with personnel files that would not survive a detailed customer audit. Others, particularly new defence suppliers and contractors taking on refinery work for the first time, need a programme built from scratch.

Atlantis supports these employers through written-practice development, drafting or revising a written practice that reflects your methods, levels, customer overlays and organisation; Level III services, including preparing and administering examinations, writing and reviewing procedures and technique sheets, and reviewing personnel records; and integrated training plans that keep classroom hours, experience logs and examinations consistent. Employer obligations are explained on our SNT-TC-1A guidance page.

For a company preparing for an audit or a new contract, we recommend updating the written practice first, then mapping personnel to methods and levels, gap-analysing records, and only then training and examining. Book a Level III consultation for your St. Louis company.

Practise before the practical exam

Many candidates understand the theory but have limited hands-on time before their practical examination. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets Atlantis trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. That mix covers St. Louis's aerospace, fabrication and refinery work.

The simulator is for practice only. It helps rehearse set-ups, scanning and indication recognition, but it does not replace the practical examination on real specimens required by your written practice, and it does not count as on-the-job experience. For written-exam revision, try the UT Level 2 practice questions and related mock-exam articles.

Your instructor

Atlantis training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He is responsible for course content, examination preparation and the Level III side of each programme, including written practices and procedures for employers. St. Louis trainees receive the same instruction and materials as all Atlantis programmes, delivered live online and onsite at the employer's facility.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in St. Louis

How do I get NDT certified in St. Louis?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete formal training, build documented experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations administered under a Level III, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and exam preparation, plus written-practice and Level III services for employers.

Can I take NDT training online in Missouri?

Yes. The theory portion of every Atlantis method course is taught live online, so trainees across Missouri and Illinois can attend. Practical training and the practical examination must be done hands-on, which we deliver onsite at the employer's facility.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in St. Louis?

No. Atlantis does not operate a physical training centre in St. Louis. Training is live online and onsite at your company's facility under ASNT Level III oversight.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice and what you already hold. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom and experience hours for each level, and experience usually takes longer than the classroom portion. See the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Missouri?

Missouri is not an Agreement State, so radiography with radioactive sources is licensed by the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission. Work on the Illinois side falls under the Illinois Emergency Management Agency. Radiographers need radiation-safety certification under 10 CFR Part 34 or the equivalent state rules. RT method certification under SNT-TC-1A is separate.

What does NDT training cost in St. Louis?

We do not publish prices. Cost depends on method, level, group size, onsite delivery and any Level III or written-practice work. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day. Request a St. Louis training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by St. Louis employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most common US framework and is widely used across St. Louis fabrication, contracting, refinery and manufacturing work. Aerospace and defence primes often add NAS 410 or customer requirements, which Atlantis does not certify to. Because certification is employer-based, a new employer recertifies you under its own written practice.

Which NDT method should I learn first in St. Louis?

For aerospace and defence suppliers, PT and MT are common starting points, followed by ET and UT. For fabrication, contracting and Metro East plants, start with VT and MT and add UT. Ask your current or target employer before you enrol.

Can one team work on both the Missouri and Illinois sides?

For most methods, yes: SNT-TC-1A certification follows the employer, not the state. Radiography is the exception, because radioactive-source work needs authorisation from the NRC in Missouri and from Illinois in Illinois.

Can our company certify its own inspectors?

Yes. Under SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies its own personnel, using a written practice, a Level III to administer or oversee examinations, and complete training and experience records. Atlantis can provide all three.

Do you offer ASNT Level III exam preparation in St. Louis?

Yes, live online, covering the Basic and method examinations. See ASNT Level III training.

Do you offer API, CWI or NAS 410 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Some St. Louis employers also ask for API inspector certifications, AWS CWI or NAS 410, which are obtained through their own schemes. Our method training complements them but does not replace them.
